Ray Kroc once said he'd stick a hose in a drowning competitor's mouth to finish the job.

Kevin Trudeau tells it straight: McDonald's founder Ray Kroc, like Rockefeller, Carnegie and Steve Jobs, built his fortune by being ruthless. Mean. Greedy. Most people hear that and decide they don't want that kind of success.

Here's the twist - you don't have to be ruthless to your competitors. You have to be ruthless with yourself. Push yourself. Be ruthless with your discipline, your persistence, your attitude.

Always be sharpening your axe, so the tool is sharp exactly when you need it.

Which part of yourself have you been going easy on?

#kevintrudeau #raykroc #mindset #richmindset #moneymindset #successhabits

'I want to be a multi-billionaire, but I'm not giving up my weekends.' Kevin Trudeau hears that one a lot.

His own dad worked a steady nine-to-five - bowling one night, cards another, fishing on weekends. A genuinely great life. But Kevin is blunt about it: his dad was never going to become a multi-billionaire, and neither will you, on that schedule.

A balanced life isn't wrong. It just has a ceiling. Ray Kroc became one of the wealthiest men alive because he was willing to do what everyone else was still just talking about.

You can have balance, or you can have extreme results. Pick one honestly.
